title: Sublinear spectral-counting exponent envelope for the normalized Green trace
question: Can the normalized Green trace be controlled by some sublinear spectral-counting exponent 0<alpha<1, rather than requiring the fixed quadratic alpha=1/2 envelope?

new_perspective.principle: For ordered positive eigenvalues lambda_k and 0<alpha<1, define C_alpha=max_k k/lambda_k^alpha. Then lambda_k >= (k/C_alpha)^(1/alpha), so tr(W^+) <= C_alpha^(1/alpha) sum_k k^(-1/alpha).
route: Evaluate several declared exponents alpha in (0,1) on every actual likelihood row.
Use the finite harmonic sum plus an integral tail bound for s=1/alpha>1, keeping the finite and infinite comparisons separate.
Select the smallest finite envelope only as a diagnostic; do not treat the selected alpha as a universal constant.
Reject alpha=1, unsorted spectra, exponent inversion and Fiedler-only shortcuts in the hostile lane.
Promote only if one exponent and its C_alpha remain bounded uniformly on a common Hamiltonian core across cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: This widens the analytic target from quadratic Weyl growth to any sublinear counting exponent. A physical promotion still requires a uniform exponent and constant, R-399 shell transfer, common-alpha dynamics and the remaining sector reconstruction.

finite_theorem.scope: The implication is finite-dimensional; neither alpha nor C_alpha is asserted uniform in cutoff, volume, phase or exhaustion.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar exponent positivity, reciprocal positivity and a finite numerical instance; ordered matrix spectra, Gibbs rows and all uniform or physical limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Prove one declared alpha in (0,1) and a positive uniform lower bound for its inverse counting constant on one Hamiltonian common core.
Control the exponent and constant under cutoff, volume, phase, source, orientation and exhaustion changes.
Transfer the resulting trace envelope to the R-399 conditional shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur residual split before any common-alpha or GNS promotion.
stop_conditions: If every tested sublinear exponent develops an unbounded C_alpha under validated stress, retain the finite comparison and register the obstruction instead of claiming a uniform trace bound.
If alpha>=1 is used, the zeta tail is divergent and the route must stop; if ordering or exponent powers are mishandled, record the exact failed inequality.
Finite sublinear counting and tail positivity are not a uniform, phase-selection, common-core, GNS, physical-gap or QFT theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite sublinear spectral-counting and zeta-tail checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform bound, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: Allowing a fitted sublinear exponent broadens the route beyond the fixed quadratic envelope; it does not establish a regulator-independent exponent or constant.
